newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia and N.Z. funds face profit pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia and N.Z. funds face profit pressure.

text.p: Fund managers in Australia and New Zealand could face significant pressure on their profitability from new entrants and price competition, accountancy firm Price Waterhouse (PW) said in its first Investment Management Survey.

PW said its survey of 17 firms in the two countries also found that it was difficult to achieve the desired economies of scale from industry mergers. It said the participating firms had A$140 billion in funds under management.

"One of the likely drivers behind the industry's interest in the sale of Commonwealth Funds Management and also Axiom has been the perceived efficiencies that should be achieved from merging two funds management operations," PW said.
"This merger/takeover acitivity in Australia reflects what has been happening on a far larger scale in the US and UK funds management markets," it said.

"Anecdotal evidence from the U.K. suggests that whilst takeover activity does deliver scale economies, the full extent of the target savings estimated when justifying a proposed deal are rarely achieved," it said.

Commonwealth Financial Services, a unit of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, agreed in December 1996 to buy the Australian government's Commonwealth Funds Management operation for an undisclosed sum. Market analysts, however, said CFM was probably sold for more than A$100 million.

The CBA unit, which participated in the survey, has also made a bid for the New South Wales government's Axiom funds unit, which has attracted the attention of Ing Groep's Mercantile Mutual local unit and the unlisted AMP Investments.
Axiom has A$17 billion under management while CFM has about A$8.0 under management.
PW said the Australia/New Zealand funds management industry was relatively profitable.

"However, we have already started to see changes that will place significant profit pressure on industry players, including new foreign entrants to the industry, greater price competition in the market, innovative products providing customers with greater flexibility and choice, more innovative pricing such as performance related fees," PW said.
